subject: English
summaryPoints: Conditional sentences maintain strict tense balance across all types: Zero conditional (general truths/rules: If + simple present, simple present/imperative), Type 1 (real future condition: If + simple present, will/can/should + base verb), Type 2 (unreal/hypothetical present: If + simple past/were, would/could/might + base verb), and Type 3 (counterfactual past: If + had + V3, would/could/might have + V3).

Participles function as adjective or adverb modifiers: present participles (-ing) indicate active or ongoing actions, while past participles (-ed/V3) represent passive, completed, or stative conditions.
A misplaced participle occurs when a participial phrase is positioned incorrectly relative to the noun it modifies, obscuring the syntactic relationship.
Correcting misplaced participles requires moving the modifying participial phrase immediately adjacent to the noun or pronoun it logically modifies.
Narrative essays rely on structured chronological sequencing, developing past events through an introduction, body paragraphs with sensory details, and an insightful concluding reflection.

Road safety data analysis in development contexts highlights high fatality rates among vulnerable road users (pedestrians, cyclists) in low- and middle-income nations due to infrastructure deficiencies and reckless driving.

formulas.label: Conditional Type 1 Formula (Real Condition)
formulas.expr: If + Subject + Simple Present (V1/-s/-es) + , + Subject + will / can / may / should + V1(base)

formulas.label: Conditional Type 2 Formula (Unreal Present)
formulas.expr: If + Subject + Simple Past (V2 / were) + , + Subject + would / could / might + V1(base)

formulas.label: Conditional Type 3 Formula (Impossible Past)
formulas.expr: If + Subject + had + V3(past participle) + , + Subject + would / could / might + have + V3(past participle)

formulas.label: Participial Phrase Placement Formula
formulas.expr: Participial Phrase (V-ing / V3) + , + Logical Subject Noun/Pronoun + Verb + Object

examTip: In EUEE conditional items, check the main clause auxiliary to identify the conditional type: if the main clause has 'would have + V3', the if-clause MUST be in the past perfect ('had + V3', Type 3). For participles, ensure the modifier immediately precedes the noun performing the action to avoid misplaced or dangling modifiers (e.g., 'Crashed, the cars were towed', NOT 'The cars were towed to the garage crashed').

keyDefinitions.definition: A non-finite verb form ending in '-ing' (present participle) or '-ed/V3' (past participle) functioning as a verbal adjective or modifier within a clause.
A participial modifier separated from the word it logically qualifies, producing an unintended, confusing, or ungrammatical meaning.
A conditional structure with simple present verbs in both clauses used to express scientific laws, universal truths, or rigid rules.
An essay genre structured chronologically to recount a sequence of events or personal experience with characters, setting, climax, and resolution.

eueeFocusTopics: Conditional Type 3 deductions ('would have been', 'could have fixed')

Identifying and correcting misplaced participial modifiers
